description: Planed dark oak, the grain unmistakable, knocked out of a Stumpling. It walked once, and now it holds shelves.
lore: Count the rings on the end grain. There are none. There is grain — beautiful grain, dark and even, straight as a ruled line — and any joiner will tell you a [[monsters/tree_stump|Stumpling]] plank works like nothing that ever grew, because nothing that ever grew is that agreeable. A tree has a bad year in it somewhere, a drought, a neighbour, a season it spent leaning. This has no years in it at all. It is exactly as much wood as a hundred thousand people were sure of, and not one splinter more.

The rule on that road is old and worth keeping. Build shelves out of it. Build a counter, a door, a bench for the fire. Do not build a bed. Whatever it eventually takes into its head to do, you want to be standing up when it does it.
gm_notes: Craft observation with a joke on the end that is not entirely a joke. Nothing has ever happened to a plank; the rule persists anyway, which is the point.
